title: TM HSBA vs TIME vs Allo: Understanding Shared vs Owned Fibre Networks
content:
If two Fibre plans offer the same 500Mbps speed, they can still perform differently because the network underneath the ISP may not be the same. In Malaysia, one important distinction is whether your ISP is using TM’s HSBA wholesale network, its own Fibre infrastructure, or another open-access network such as Allo.

The difference matters most when you look beyond the advertised Mbps.

TM HSBA: What Does “Wholesale Fibre” Actually Mean?

HSBA (High-Speed Broadband Access) is a wholesale service that allows other broadband providers to use TM’s HSBB network to deliver broadband services without building the entire access network themselves.

TM has been a major wholesale infrastructure provider for Malaysia’s broadband industry. TM has stated that its wholesale business supports multiple local broadband providers through HSBA, with more than 670,000 ports delivered to five local broadband providers in one of its reported periods.

(Source: TM — TM Wholesale supports the telco/technology growth in Malaysia & region)

TM official source

This is why you can have different brands selling Fibre broadband while the physical access network to your home may still be provided by TM.

For example, Maxis confirms that its agreement with TM allows it to access TM's national Fibre network, while also complementing this with Maxis' own-build Fibre infrastructure.

(Source: Maxis — Maxis Leverages TM’s High-speed Broadband Services to Drive Digital Adoption Nationwide)

Maxis official source

So the important question is not simply:

“Which ISP am I subscribing to?”

It is:

“Whose access network is actually carrying my connection?”

Shared Network Does Not Automatically Mean Slow

This is where many Fibre comparisons go wrong.

A wholesale network does not mean every customer is permanently sharing one small pipe.

Malaysia's regulated HSBB framework includes Layer 2 HSBB Network Service with QoS, where the access provider supplies connectivity between the customer's premises and a Point of Interconnection (POI), while the access seeker selects the bit rate and QoS class.

(Source: Allo Reference Access Offer — Layer 2 HSBB Network Service with QoS)

Allo official RAO document

The actual performance therefore depends on how the ISP engineers the network around that wholesale connection.

A customer can have a perfectly healthy 500Mbps access connection but still experience poor performance because congestion occurs further upstream.

Think of Fibre as several sections:

Home → Access Network → Aggregation → ISP Core → Internet Exchange/Peering → International Network → Destination

Congestion at any one of these points can affect the final experience.

Why Can Some TM-Based Fibre Services Slow Down During Peak Hours?

The important word is capacity.

During peak hours — typically when many households are streaming, gaming, downloading and working online simultaneously — traffic increases dramatically.

If an ISP's available capacity at an aggregation, upstream, peering or international transit point is insufficient, customers can experience:

  1. Lower speed-test results
  2. Higher latency
  3. Packet loss
  4. Slower international downloads
  5. Buffering on certain services
  6. Gaming ping spikes

But this should not automatically be blamed on TM HSBA.

A TM-based ISP can invest heavily in additional upstream and international capacity and perform very well. Conversely, an ISP operating on its own Fibre network can still experience congestion if its own upstream capacity is poorly provisioned.

That is why “TM Fibre = congested” is an oversimplification.

TIME: More Control Because It Owns the Fibre Network

TIME is a different model in areas where its own Fibre infrastructure is available.

TIME explicitly states that it owns its Fibre network and operates a 100% Fibre network. It also says its network is monitored and optimised to provide consistent performance during peak hours or heavy usage.

(Source: TIME — Our Fibre Network)

TIME official Fibre network page

TIME's corporate information also describes its domestic network as a fully-fibre network built around its Cross Peninsular Cable System (CPCS).

(Source: TIME — Who We Are)

TIME corporate official page

The advantage is network control.

TIME controls more of the infrastructure between the customer and its own network core instead of depending entirely on another operator's last-mile access network.

That gives TIME greater control over:

  1. Network capacity
  2. Access network upgrades
  3. Network engineering
  4. Fault management
  5. Expansion
  6. Traffic optimisation

However, this does not mean TIME is physically independent from every other network.

Internet traffic still eventually depends on data centres, peering networks, submarine cables and international carriers.

Allo: A Different Kind of “Owned Network”

Allo is particularly interesting because it is both an infrastructure operator and an open-access Fibre network provider.

Allo is a wholly owned subsidiary of TNB and says its network is an open-access, full-fibre infrastructure designed to serve households, SMEs, enterprises and carriers.

(Source: Allo — About Allo)

Allo official corporate page

Allo also describes its network as its “own Internet highway” and promotes a low-contention-ratio Fibre service.

(Source: Allo — Allo Fibre for Enterprise)

Allo official Fibre page

Its wholesale network is built around TNB's extensive fibre infrastructure, with Allo stating that it has access to approximately 25,000km of TNB assets across Peninsular Malaysia.

(Source: Allo — Wholesale Services)

Allo official wholesale network page

So Allo should not simply be described as “another ISP”.

It is also a network infrastructure provider that other service providers can use.

For example, Maxis previously signed an agreement with Allo to use Allo's HSBB network services, with Allo providing access infrastructure up to the customer's premises while Maxis managed the retail and service side.

(Source: Maxis — Maxis continues to accelerate fiberisation in Malaysia with Allo partnership)

Maxis official source

That proves an important point:

Owned network and wholesale network are not mutually exclusive.

An infrastructure owner can also be a wholesale provider.

TM HSBA vs TIME vs Allo

NetworkBasic ModelWho Controls Access Network?Wholesale AccessMain Advantage
TM HSBAWholesale HSBB accessTMYesVery wide coverage and mature infrastructure
TIMEOwn Fibre networkTIMEYes, in certain wholesale arrangementsGreater end-to-end network control
AlloOwn/open-access Fibre infrastructureAlloYesOpen-access model with TNB fibre infrastructure

The biggest difference is therefore not simply speed.

It is who controls the infrastructure underneath the retail broadband service.

Why Network Ownership Matters During Peak Hours

Suppose three customers buy 500Mbps plans.

Customer A uses an ISP riding on TM HSBA.

Customer B uses an ISP on TIME's network.

Customer C uses an ISP on Allo's network.

All three may see approximately 500Mbps on a good speed test.

But at 9pm, their experience can diverge.

Why?

Because the 500Mbps advertised to the customer is only the access speed.

The ISP still has to provide enough capacity beyond the access network.

A simplified example:

500Mbps home plan

→ Fibre access

→ Aggregation

→ ISP core

→ Peering / Internet Exchange

→ International transit

→ Netflix / YouTube / game server / website

If the bottleneck occurs at the ISP's international transit, changing from TM to TIME will not automatically fix it.

If the bottleneck is inside the access network, however, having greater control over that infrastructure can make a significant difference.

This is where an owned network becomes strategically valuable.

Does TIME or Allo Guarantee No Peak-Hour Congestion?

No.

This is an important distinction for consumers.

TIME explicitly markets its own network as providing consistent performance during peak hours, while Allo promotes its own Fibre infrastructure and low contention ratio. These are advantages, but they should not be interpreted as a guarantee that every customer in every location will experience identical performance.

(Source: TIME — Our Fibre Network)

TIME official source

(Source: Allo — Allo Fibre for Enterprise)

Allo official source

Your actual experience can still depend on:

  1. Local network capacity
  2. ISP aggregation capacity
  3. International bandwidth
  4. Peering arrangements
  5. CDN availability
  6. Routing to the destination server
  7. Network maintenance or faults

This is why two customers using the same ISP can sometimes report completely different experiences.

How to Tell Whether Your ISP Uses TM HSBA, TIME or Allo

This is more useful than looking at the ISP brand alone.

Some providers operate across multiple underlying networks.

Maxis, for example, explicitly lists TM-HSBA, Allo and TIME among the network providers available through its Fibre ecosystem.

(Source: Maxis — List of Providers)

Maxis Fibre network provider list

CelcomDigi has also announced arrangements to use TIME's Fibre infrastructure for its Fibre offerings, particularly in condominiums and apartments.

(Source: CelcomDigi — CelcomDigi and Time dotCom collaborate to boost fibre accessibility for Malaysians)

CelcomDigi official announcement

So the same retail brand may use different underlying networks depending on your address.

That means checking the available network at your specific property can be more useful than simply asking:

“Is Maxis Fibre good?”

The better question is:

“Which Fibre network will Maxis use at my address?”

What Should You Choose?

Choose a TM HSBA-based service if:

  1. TM has the strongest coverage at your address
  2. You want more ISP choices
  3. The ISP has good local and international capacity
  4. Your area has a reliable track record
  5. The price is significantly better

TM's biggest advantage remains scale and coverage.

Consider TIME if:

  1. TIME's own Fibre is available at your address
  2. You prioritise network control
  3. You care about upload performance
  4. You frequently use cloud services, gaming, video calls or large uploads

TIME's own network can be particularly attractive where its coverage is available.

Consider Allo if:

  1. Allo's network is available at your address
  2. You want an alternative Fibre infrastructure
  3. You are comparing providers that use different underlying networks
  4. Your area has good Allo coverage and competitive retail plans

Allo's open-access model also means the retail ISP and physical network provider may be different companies.

NetBijak's Take

Don't judge a Fibre plan by the ISP logo alone.

The more important question is:

Who owns the Fibre network at your address, and where does that ISP connect to the wider Internet?

TM HSBA gives Malaysia extensive wholesale Fibre access and allows multiple providers to reach customers without building an entirely separate access network.

TIME has the advantage of greater control over its own Fibre infrastructure.

Allo takes another approach by operating an open-access Fibre infrastructure based on TNB's network assets.

But network ownership alone does not determine whether your Internet will be fast at 9pm.

For consumers, the best Fibre connection is the combination of:

Good access network + sufficient ISP capacity + strong peering + good routing + reliable local infrastructure.

So when comparing broadband plans on NetBijak, don't stop at 100Mbps vs 300Mbps vs 1Gbps.

The more useful comparison is:

Retail ISP → Underlying Fibre Network → Network Capacity → Peering/Routing → Actual user experience.

That is where the real difference between Fibre providers starts to become visible.

ai_summary: Choosing a fibre broadband plan in Malaysia requires understanding that the quality of your connection depends on which physical network carries your traffic. While many providers use TM’s HSBA wholesale infrastructure, performance issues during peak hours are often caused by how an individual ISP manages its own upstream capacity rather than the shared network itself. TIME offers a different experience by owning and operating its own dedicated fibre infrastructure, which provides the company with greater control over network engineering and traffic optimization. Meanwhile, Allo acts as an open-access provider leveraging TNB’s extensive assets to offer its own unique network highway to various retail service providers. Ultimately, advertised speeds are only part of the equation, as network architecture and capacity management play critical roles in your actual online experience. Because of these differences, consumers should look beyond the Mbps figure to understand the underlying infrastructure supporting their connection.

title: Pemasangan Fibre Melintasi Rumah Jiran: Cara Selesaikan Pertikaian di Malaysia
content:
Jika Installer Fibre memberitahu bahawa kabel perlu melalui bumbung, pokok atau kawasan rumah jiran untuk menyambungkan Fibre ke rumah anda, jangan terus bergaduh dengan jiran dan jangan terus setuju dengan laluan tersebut.

Minta ISP rekodkan masalah itu, semak sama ada terdapat Pole atau Distribution Point (DP) lain, dan buat technical route assessment sebelum pemasangan diteruskan.

Perkara paling penting: jangan anggap bahawa MCMC mempunyai satu peraturan mudah yang melarang semua kabel Fibre daripada melintasi rumah jiran.

Dalam situasi sebenar, isu ini boleh melibatkan network design ISP, lokasi Pole dan DP, installation standards, akses ke kawasan persendirian serta sama ada terdapat laluan lain yang secara teknikalnya boleh digunakan.

Kenapa Kabel Fibre Perlu Melalui Rumah Jiran?

Untuk rumah teres, Fibre biasanya disambungkan daripada network infrastructure yang sedia ada.

Fibre Distribution Point (DP) mungkin berada pada Pole di hadapan rumah lain, bukannya tepat di hadapan rumah anda.

Sebab itu Installer mungkin berdepan keadaan seperti:

  1. DP terletak di Pole rumah jiran;
  2. laluan paling pendek terhalang oleh pokok;
  3. terdapat jalan atau longkang antara Pole dan rumah;
  4. Fibre infrastructure sedia ada berada di lokasi tertentu;
  5. aerial route paling mudah memerlukan kabel melalui atas sebahagian rumah jiran.

Ini boleh menyebabkan Installer mencadangkan laluan:

Pole → atas rumah jiran → rumah anda

Tetapi satu perkara perlu difahami:

Laluan yang paling mudah untuk Installer tidak semestinya satu-satunya laluan yang boleh digunakan.

Jika laluan tersebut menimbulkan pertikaian, minta ISP buat technical route assessment.

Adakah MCMC Melarang Kabel Fibre Melintasi Rumah Jiran?

Bahagian ini perlu dijelaskan dengan tepat.

Setakat maklumat rasmi yang boleh disahkan, tidak terdapat satu peraturan pengguna MCMC yang mudah difahami sebagai:

“Kabel Fibre tidak boleh melintasi rumah jiran.”

Jadi, NetBijak tidak mengesyorkan pengguna memberitahu ISP bahawa:

“MCMC melarang Fibre melintasi rumah jiran.”

Itu terlalu umum.

Sebaliknya, isu ini boleh dikemukakan sebagai installation dan service-delivery dispute.

CFM menyediakan saluran aduan untuk isu komunikasi termasuk Service Delivery, Terms & Conditions Disputes dan Unfair Practice.

(Source: CFM — Complaint Channels)

CFM — Complaint Channels (cfm.my)

Soalan yang lebih tepat kepada ISP ialah:

“Adakah laluan ini benar-benar satu-satunya laluan yang boleh digunakan? Adakah Pole, DP atau Fibre route lain telah diperiksa?”

Kalau Fibre Perlu Melalui Bumbung Rumah Jiran?

Ini antara situasi yang paling mudah menyebabkan pertikaian antara jiran.

Sebelum Installer mula bekerja, semak dahulu:

  1. Fibre datang dari Pole atau DP mana?
  2. Kabel akan melalui atas bumbung jiran atau tidak?
  3. Kabel akan dipasang pada struktur rumah jiran?
  4. Adakah kerja maintenance pada masa depan memerlukan akses ke rumah jiran?
  5. Adakah terdapat Pole atau DP lain?
  6. Adakah aerial route lain boleh digunakan?
  7. Adakah underground Fibre boleh dibuat?
  8. Adakah ISP sudah membuat alternative route assessment?

Ambil gambar keadaan sebenar.

Pastikan gambar menunjukkan:

Pole → DP → Bumbung jiran → Pokok → Rumah anda → Property Boundary

Kemudian hantarkan kepada ISP.

Anda boleh gunakan ayat ini:

“The proposed Fibre route crosses a neighbouring private property. Please arrange a technical route assessment and advise whether an alternative pole, Distribution Point (DP) or Fibre route is available.”

Ini jauh lebih berkesan daripada hanya berkata:

“Saya tak nak kabel lalu rumah jiran.”

Bagaimana Jika Pokok Jiran Menghalang Laluan Fibre?

Pokok boleh menjadi masalah jangka panjang.

Hari ini mungkin masih ada ruang antara dahan dan kabel. Tetapi beberapa tahun kemudian:

  1. dahan boleh menyentuh Fibre cable;
  2. dahan boleh jatuh ketika hujan atau ribut;
  3. kerja potong pokok boleh merosakkan Fibre;
  4. kabel boleh bergesel dengan dahan;
  5. kerja repair menjadi lebih susah.

Jika Installer mahu membawa Fibre melalui atau berhampiran pokok besar milik jiran, tanya:

  1. Adakah kabel akan bersentuhan dengan pokok?
  2. Adakah clearance mencukupi?
  3. Adakah laluan lain boleh digunakan?
  4. Siapa bertanggungjawab jika kabel rosak akibat pokok?
  5. Adakah pokok perlu dipangkas?

Jangan potong pokok jiran sendiri.

Jika kerja pemasangan memerlukan perubahan pada pokok atau kawasan milik orang lain, perkara itu perlu dijelaskan dengan ISP dan pemilik berkenaan terlebih dahulu.

Boleh Minta ISP Tukar Laluan Pole?

Boleh minta ISP buat penilaian laluan alternatif.

Tetapi ini tidak bermaksud ISP wajib memasang Pole baru hanya kerana lokasi Pole sedia ada menyusahkan anda.

Anda boleh minta ISP periksa:

  1. Pole lain;
  2. DP lain;
  3. aerial route lain;
  4. surface cabling;
  5. underground cabling;
  6. kemungkinan Pole relocation.

Sebab itu jangan hanya tulis:

“Move the pole.”

Lebih baik gunakan:

“The current pole position requires the proposed Fibre cable to cross a neighbouring private property. Please assess whether another pole, DP or network route can be used, and advise whether pole relocation is technically feasible.”

Dengan cara ini, isu anda boleh dinaikkan kepada technical/network team, bukan berhenti pada Installer sahaja.

Bagaimana Unifi Mengklasifikasikan Installation?

Panduan pemasangan rasmi Unifi menunjukkan perbezaan antara Standard dan Non-Standard Installation.

Pole → Entry Wall secara terus

→ Standard Installation

→ Disediakan oleh TM

Manakala:

Pole → Entry Wall melalui underground + surface cabling

→ Non-Standard Installation

→ Kos ditanggung pelanggan

→ Caj cabling yang dinyatakan ketika ini ialah RM212.

(Source: Unifi — Home Broadband Installation Journey)

Unifi — Home Broadband Installation Journey (unifi.com.my)

Ini penting kerana:

Laluan alternatif tidak semestinya bermaksud pemasangan itu percuma.

Jika ISP menawarkan laluan lain dengan caj tambahan, tanya dahulu:

  1. Apakah installation method?
  2. Kenapa ia dikategorikan sebagai Non-Standard?
  3. Kerja apa yang perlu dibuat?
  4. Berapa panjang kabel?
  5. Perlu underground work?
  6. Perlu surface cabling?
  7. Ada caj tambahan lain?

Bagaimana Dengan Maxis Fibre?

Maxis juga membezakan antara Standard dan Non-Standard Installation.

Menurut FAQ pemasangan Fibre Maxis, Standard Installation secara umum meliputi sehingga 100 meter dari Fibre Distribution Panel terdekat ke modem, menggunakan kaedah pemasangan standard seperti kabel di atas dinding menggunakan clips.

Kaedah seperti underground ducts, concealed wiring dan over-ceiling cabling boleh dikategorikan sebagai Non-Standard dan mungkin dikenakan caj tambahan.

(Source: Maxis — Fibre Installation FAQs)

Maxis — Fibre Installation FAQs (maxis.com.my)

Jadi jika laluan pemasangan rumah anda tidak normal, soalan penting ialah:

“Adakah ini Standard Installation atau Non-Standard Installation?”

Kalau Jiran Tidak Setuju?

Jika jiran jelas tidak membenarkan kabel Fibre melalui bumbung atau kawasan rumah mereka, jangan paksa pemasangan.

Beritahu ISP:

“The neighbouring property owner does not agree to the proposed Fibre route. Please assess whether an alternative pole, DP or Fibre route is available.”

Minta perkara ini direkodkan dalam Installation Ticket.

Ini penting supaya masalah tersebut mempunyai rekod rasmi:

Proposed route melibatkan kawasan jiran → jiran tidak bersetuju → pelanggan meminta alternative route.

Jika ISP kemudian berkata tiada laluan lain, tanya:

  1. Adakah Pole lain telah diperiksa?
  2. Adakah DP lain telah diperiksa?
  3. Adakah aerial route lain telah dinilai?
  4. Boleh guna underground route?
  5. Boleh guna surface cabling?
  6. Adakah laluan alternatif akan dikenakan caj?

Boleh Minta Pole Baru?

Anda boleh memintanya, tetapi lebih baik minta technical assessment, bukannya terus menuntut Pole baru.

Contohnya:

“Please assess whether pole relocation is technically feasible because the current pole position requires the Fibre cable to cross a neighbouring private property.”

Pole merupakan sebahagian daripada network infrastructure, jadi ISP perlu menentukan sama ada relocation benar-benar sesuai berdasarkan network design dan technical feasibility.

Bagaimana Jika Installer Kata “Ini Satu-Satunya Laluan”?

Jangan terus anggap keputusan itu muktamad.

Installer biasanya bekerja berdasarkan infrastructure yang tersedia dan installation instructions untuk kawasan tersebut.

Jika masalah melibatkan:

  1. jiran;
  2. bumbung;
  3. pokok;
  4. private property;
  5. Pole;
  6. DP;
  7. alternative route;

minta isu itu dinaikkan kepada technical/network team.

Gunakan ayat:

“Please escalate this installation for a technical route assessment. The proposed cable route crosses a neighbouring private property, and the property owner does not agree to the proposed route. Please confirm whether another pole, DP or Fibre route has been assessed.”

Matlamatnya ialah supaya keputusan dibuat oleh pihak yang melihat network route secara keseluruhan, bukan sekadar berdasarkan apa yang paling mudah dibuat oleh Installer di lokasi.

Adakah Laluan Alternatif Akan Dikenakan Caj?

Mungkin.

Unifi secara rasmi menyatakan sesetengah underground + surface cabling sebagai Non-Standard Installation dengan caj cabling RM212.

(Source: Unifi — Home Broadband Installation Journey)

Unifi — Installation Guide (unifi.com.my)

Maxis pula menyatakan sesetengah Non-Standard Installation seperti underground ducts dan concealed wiring boleh dikenakan caj tambahan.

(Source: Maxis — Fibre Installation FAQs)

Maxis — Fibre Installation FAQ (maxis.com.my)

Sebelum bersetuju, minta ISP sahkan:

  1. Installation Method;
  2. Cable Length;
  3. Underground / Surface Work;
  4. sama ada Pole baru diperlukan;
  5. jumlah caj tambahan;
  6. siapa yang menjalankan kerja tersebut.

Jangan hanya bergantung pada quotation lisan.

Bukti Apa Yang Perlu Disimpan?

Jika anda percaya laluan Fibre tersebut bermasalah, ambil gambar sebelum Installer meninggalkan rumah.

Simpan:

Gambar Pole

Tunjukkan Pole dan rumah di sekeliling.

Gambar DP

Jika boleh dilihat dan selamat untuk diambil gambar.

Gambar Proposed Cable Route

Tunjukkan dengan jelas laluan yang Installer cadangkan.

Gambar Pokok / Bumbung

Jika ia menjadi punca pertikaian.

Property Boundary

Tunjukkan kenapa laluan tersebut melibatkan kawasan jiran.

Rekod Komunikasi

Simpan:

  1. WhatsApp;
  2. SMS;
  3. Email;
  4. Installation Ticket;
  5. Order Number;
  6. jawapan Installer;
  7. jawapan Customer Service;
  8. quotation;
  9. gambar.

Dokumentasi ini sangat berguna jika aduan perlu dinaikkan kemudian.

Bila Perlu Buat Aduan Kepada MCMC?

Beri ISP peluang yang munasabah untuk menyelesaikan masalah terlebih dahulu.

Jika masih tidak selesai, anda boleh menggunakan saluran aduan pengguna MCMC/CFM.

CFM menyenaraikan Service Delivery dan Terms & Conditions Disputes antara kategori aduan berkaitan perkhidmatan komunikasi.

(Source: CFM — Complaint Channels)

CFM — Complaint Channels (cfm.my)

Aduan boleh dibuat melalui MCMC Consumer Redress Portal atau menghubungi:

MCMC Consumer Care Centre: 1800-188-030

(Source: CFM — New Complaint)

CFM — New Complaint / MCMC Consumer Redress Portal (cfm.my)

Jangan hanya tulis:

“ISP tak mahu pasang Fibre.”

Terangkan kronologi.

Contohnya:

“Saya telah memohon pemasangan Fibre. Installer mencadangkan laluan aerial yang melintasi kawasan persendirian jiran. Pemilik rumah jiran tidak bersetuju dengan laluan tersebut. Saya telah meminta alternative pole, DP atau technical route assessment, tetapi masalah masih belum diselesaikan.”

Lampirkan:

gambar + Ticket Number + WhatsApp + Email + jawapan ISP.

Ini memberikan gambaran yang jauh lebih jelas kepada pihak yang mengendalikan aduan.

Adakah MCMC Akan Paksa ISP Pasang Pole Baru?

Jangan anggap begitu.

Saluran aduan membolehkan masalah perkhidmatan anda disemak, tetapi ini tidak bermaksud MCMC secara automatik akan mengarahkan ISP memasang Pole baru di lokasi yang anda pilih.

Penyelesaian sebenar masih bergantung kepada:

  1. network infrastructure;
  2. lokasi DP;
  3. technical feasibility;
  4. installation standard;
  5. property access;
  6. construction requirements;
  7. kelulusan yang berkaitan.

CFM menerangkan bahawa peranannya termasuk menyediakan saluran aduan dan membantu mengendalikan isu pengguna berdasarkan rangka kerja pengguna yang berkaitan.

(Source: CFM — About Us)

CFM — About Us (cfm.my)

Jadi objektif aduan adalah untuk mendapatkan penyelesaian dan jawapan rasmi daripada ISP, bukannya menganggap regulator akan mereka semula network Fibre untuk rumah anda.

Apa Yang Anda Jangan Buat

Jangan potong Fibre Cable

Walaupun anda tidak suka laluan kabel tersebut, jangan potong atau rosakkan Fibre infrastructure.

Jangan alihkan Pole sendiri

Pole ialah network infrastructure. Minta ISP menilai relocation.

Jangan potong pokok jiran

Masalah Fibre tidak memberikan anda hak untuk mengubah harta jiran.

Jangan benarkan pemasangan dahulu

Jika anda sudah tahu laluan tersebut dipertikaikan, selesaikan isu sebelum pemasangan.

Jangan hanya bergaduh dengan Installer

Jika isu melibatkan Pole, DP, jiran atau alternative route, minta technical/network team ISP masuk campur.

Langkah Penyelesaian Yang Paling Praktikal

Jika pemasangan Fibre anda terhalang kerana melibatkan rumah jiran, ikut langkah ini:

1. Ambil gambar proposed route

Pole, DP, bumbung, pokok dan property boundary.

2. Minta Installer rekodkan masalah

Pastikan Installation Ticket menunjukkan sebab pemasangan tidak dapat diteruskan.

3. Hubungi ISP

Terangkan bahawa proposed route melibatkan private property jiran.

4. Minta technical route assessment

Tanya secara spesifik tentang Pole, DP dan Fibre route lain.

5. Tanya tentang alternative installation

Contohnya Surface atau Underground Cabling.

6. Minta jumlah caj

Terutamanya jika dikategorikan sebagai Non-Standard Installation.

7. Simpan semua rekod

WhatsApp, Email, Ticket, quotation dan gambar.

8. Eskalasi kepada MCMC/CFM jika masih tidak selesai

Hantar kronologi dan semua bukti yang berkaitan.

Template Untuk Hantar Kepada ISP

Jika anda menggunakan Unifi, Maxis atau ISP Fibre lain, anda boleh hantar mesej ini:

“The proposed Fibre installation route crosses a neighbouring private property / roof / tree, and the property owner does not agree to the proposed route. Please arrange a technical route assessment and advise whether an alternative pole, Distribution Point (DP), aerial route or other Fibre route is available. If an alternative installation is considered non-standard, please provide the installation method and applicable charges before proceeding.”

Kuncinya ialah minta technical route assessment, bukan sekadar meminta Customer Service “ubah kabel”.

NetBijak's Take

Masalah Fibre yang melibatkan rumah jiran sepatutnya dilihat sebagai network route dan installation issue, bukannya pergaduhan antara jiran.

Setakat maklumat rasmi yang tersedia, tidak wajar untuk memberitahu pengguna bahawa:

“MCMC melarang Fibre Cable melintasi rumah jiran.”

Itu terlalu umum dan tidak disokong oleh satu peraturan pengguna MCMC yang jelas seperti itu.

Cara yang lebih praktikal ialah:

Ambil bukti → minta ISP semak semula laluan → tanya Pole / DP lain → minta Alternative Route → semak caj Non-Standard Installation → eskalasi kepada MCMC/CFM jika tidak selesai.

Jika Fibre route melibatkan bumbung, pokok atau kawasan persendirian jiran, jangan potong kabel, jangan alihkan Pole dan jangan ubah pokok jiran sendiri.

Ayat paling kuat kepada ISP bukan:

“MCMC kata kabel ini tak boleh lalu sini.”

Sebaliknya:

“The proposed route crosses a neighbouring private property. Please conduct a technical route assessment and confirm whether an alternative pole, DP or Fibre route is available.”

Dengan cara ini, ISP perlu menjawab persoalan yang sebenar:

Adakah terdapat laluan lain yang secara teknikal boleh digunakan?

🎯Cari Pelan Saya →

ai_summary: Jika pemasangan kabel fibre memerlukan laluan melalui kawasan atau bumbung rumah jiran, jangan terus bersetuju atau mencetuskan pertikaian dengan jiran tersebut. Sebaiknya, minta pihak ISP melakukan penilaian laluan teknikal bagi mengenal pasti sama ada terdapat alternatif lain yang lebih sesuai tanpa perlu melanggar ruang persendirian. Perlu difahami bahawa tiada peraturan khusus MCMC yang secara mutlak melarang kabel melintasi rumah jiran, namun anda berhak meminta ISP memeriksa ketersediaan tiang atau titik pengagihan lain. Semasa proses perbincangan, ambil gambar keadaan tapak pemasangan untuk dijadikan bukti bagi menyokong permintaan anda kepada pihak ISP. Sekiranya laluan alternatif dikategorikan sebagai pemasangan bukan standard, anda perlu bertanya dengan jelas mengenai caj tambahan yang mungkin dikenakan oleh pihak penyedia perkhidmatan. Pendekatan profesional dengan pihak ISP adalah kunci utama bagi menyelesaikan isu ini secara berkesan tanpa merosakkan hubungan kejiranan.

title: Fibre 安装跨过邻居屋顶怎么办？马来西亚消费者如何解决纠纷
content:
如果 Fibre 安装人员告诉你，要把 Fibre cable 拉过邻居屋顶、树木甚至私人范围才能接入你家，不要急着和邻居吵，也不要马上接受这个路线。 先要求 ISP 记录施工情况，并检查是否可以通过其他 Pole、Distribution Point（DP）或 Fibre 路线接入。

这里最容易出现的误解是：很多人以为 “MCMC 规定 Fibre 不能跨邻居屋顶”。

目前并没有找到这样一条简单、统一的 MCMC 消费者规定。

实际问题通常涉及 ISP 的网络设计、现有 Pole/DP、installation standard、私人范围的 access，以及有没有其他技术上可行的路线。

为什么 Fibre 会需要经过邻居屋顶？

排屋（terrace house）的 Fibre 通常不是直接从你家门口开始铺。

网络可能从附近的 Fibre Distribution Point（DP）或 Pole 接出来，而 DP 的位置不一定刚好就在你家的正前方。

例如：

  1. 最近的 DP 在隔壁家的 Pole；
  2. 你的房子与 Pole 之间有排屋、沟渠或道路；
  3. 最短路线被大树挡住；
  4. 现有 Fibre infrastructure 的位置有限；
  5. Installer 根据现有 network route 选择 aerial cable。

于是就可能出现：

Pole → 邻居房屋上方 → 你的房子

这种情况。

但要注意：

Installer 能够拉过去，不代表这就是唯一可行路线。

所以遇到争议时，第一步不是和邻居争论，而是要求 ISP 做 technical route assessment。

MCMC 有没有规定 Fibre 不能跨邻居私人范围？

这点必须讲清楚。

目前没有找到一条可以简单理解为：

“Fibre cable 绝对不能跨过邻居私人土地或屋顶。”

的 MCMC 消费者规定。

因此，NetBijak 不建议消费者直接拿“MCMC 禁止跨界拉 Fibre”去和 ISP 或 Installer 理论。

比较准确的做法，是把问题当成 Fibre installation / service delivery dispute 处理。

CFM 的消费者投诉渠道涵盖包括 Service Delivery、Terms & Conditions Disputes、Unfair Practice 等通讯服务问题。

(Source: CFM — Complaint Channels)

CFM — Complaint Channels (cfm.my)

所以真正应该问 ISP 的问题是：

“这个路线是不是唯一技术上可行的路线？有没有检查过其他 Pole、DP 或 Fibre route？”

如果 Fibre Cable 要跨过邻居屋顶怎么办？

这是排屋最容易发生纠纷的情况之一。

先不要让 Installer 直接开工。

确认以下几个问题：

  1. Fibre 从哪一个 Pole / DP 出来？
  2. Cable 会不会直接经过邻居屋顶？
  3. Cable 会不会固定在邻居房屋上？
  4. 以后维修是否需要进入邻居家？
  5. 有没有其他 Pole 或 DP？
  6. 有没有其他 aerial route？
  7. Underground Fibre 是否可行？
  8. ISP 有没有做过 alternative route assessment？

建议先拍照。

最好把以下位置拍清楚：

Pole → DP → 邻居屋顶 → 树木 → 你的房子 → Property Boundary

然后把照片交给 ISP。

你可以这样要求：

“The proposed Fibre route crosses a neighbouring private property. Please arrange a technical route assessment and advise whether an alternative pole, Distribution Point (DP) or Fibre route is available.”

这比单纯告诉客服：

“我不要 Fibre 经过邻居家。”

有效得多。

如果是邻居的树挡住 Fibre 路线呢？

树的问题比屋顶更加复杂，因为树会继续生长。

现在没有碰到 Cable，不代表几年后不会碰到。

长期可能出现：

  1. 树枝压到 Fibre cable；
  2. 大风导致树枝碰撞 Cable；
  3. 修树时误伤 Fibre；
  4. Cable 与树枝长期摩擦；
  5. 维修人员无法安全接近 Cable。

如果 Installer 要把 Fibre 拉过邻居的大树，先问清楚：

  1. Cable 会不会接触树枝？
  2. 是否有足够 clearance？
  3. 有没有其他路线？
  4. 如果以后树枝损坏 Cable，由谁负责？
  5. 是否需要修剪树木？

不要自己去砍邻居的树。

如果施工真的需要修改邻居范围内的树木，应先由 ISP 和相关屋主处理。

可以要求 ISP 换 Pole 吗？

可以要求，但不代表 ISP 一定必须换。

这是两个不同的问题。

你可以要求 ISP：

  1. 检查附近其他 Pole；
  2. 检查其他 DP；
  3. 重新设计 aerial route；
  4. 检查 surface cabling；
  5. 检查 underground cabling；
  6. 评估 Pole relocation。

但 ISP 是否真的可以更换 Pole，要看 network design 和技术可行性。

因此不要只说：

“Move the pole.”

更好的说法是：

“The current pole position requires the proposed Fibre cable to cross a neighbouring private property. Please assess whether another pole, DP or network route can be used, and advise whether pole relocation is technically feasible.”

这样 ISP 才会把问题交给真正负责 network planning 的团队。

Unifi 的 Standard Installation 怎么算？

Unifi 官方目前对不同 Fibre installation 方法有明确区分。

其中：

Pole → Entry Wall 的直接 Cable

属于 Standard Installation，由 TM 提供。

而：

Pole → Entry Wall，需要经过 underground + surface cabling

则属于 Non-Standard Installation，官方页面目前列出的 Cabling Charge 是 RM212。

(Source: Unifi — Home Broadband Installation Journey)

Unifi — Home Broadband Installation Journey (unifi.com.my)

这说明一个很重要的问题：

有 Alternative Route，不代表 Alternative Route 一定免费。

所以如果客服告诉你：

“可以换路线，但要另外收费。”

不要马上答应。

先问清楚：

  1. 什么 Installation Method？
  2. 为什么属于 Non-Standard？
  3. 需要什么工程？
  4. Cable 多长？
  5. 是否需要 underground work？
  6. 是否需要 Surface Cabling？
  7. 有没有其他额外费用？

Maxis Fibre 又是怎样？

Maxis 同样区分 Standard Installation 和 Non-Standard Installation。

Maxis 官方资料说明，其 Standard Installation 一般涵盖从最近的 Fibre Distribution Panel 到 Modem 的首 100 metres，并包括例如沿墙使用 clips 的标准布线方式。

如果需要超过标准范围，或者使用 underground ducts、concealed wiring、over-ceiling cabling 等方式，则可能产生额外费用。

(Source: Maxis — Fibre Installation FAQs)

Maxis — Fibre Installation FAQs (maxis.com.my)

所以无论是 Unifi、Maxis 还是其他 Fibre ISP，遇到特殊路线时都应该先问：

这是 Standard Installation，还是 Non-Standard Installation？

如果邻居不同意怎么办？

如果邻居明确表示不允许 Fibre Cable 经过他的屋顶或私人范围，不要强行施工。

直接告诉 ISP：

“The neighbouring property owner does not agree to the proposed Fibre route. Please assess whether an alternative pole, DP or Fibre route is available.”

然后要求客服把这个情况记录在 Installation Ticket。

这样以后如果问题升级，你可以证明：

不是你拒绝 Fibre installation，而是 proposed route 涉及邻居私人范围，因此要求 ISP 提供其他方案。

如果 ISP 回复：

“没有其他路线。”

继续问：

  1. 有没有检查其他 Pole？
  2. 有没有检查其他 DP？
  3. 有没有检查其他 aerial route？
  4. Underground route 是否可行？
  5. Surface cabling 是否可行？
  6. Alternative route 是否需要额外收费？

如果要申请更换 Fibre Pole 呢？

可以申请，但不要把它写成：

“我要求你们一定要搬 Pole。”

比较合理的写法是：

“Please assess whether pole relocation is technically feasible because the current pole position requires the Fibre cable to cross a neighbouring private property.”

重点是 request an assessment。

因为 Pole 属于 network infrastructure，ISP 需要从网络规划、现有基础设施以及施工可行性判断是否能够更换。

如果 Installer 说：“只有这一条路线。”

不要马上认为事情就结束了。

Installer 通常是按照现场已有 infrastructure 和 installation instruction 工作。

如果涉及：

  1. 邻居不同意；
  2. 屋顶；
  3. 树木；
  4. 私人范围；
  5. Pole；
  6. Alternative Route；

就应该要求 ISP 的 technical/network team 重新评估。

可以直接这样写：

“Please escalate this installation for a technical route assessment. The proposed cable route crosses a neighbouring private property, and the property owner does not agree to the proposed route. Please confirm whether another pole, DP or Fibre route has been assessed.”

这比一直和 Installer 争论有效得多。

Alternative Route 要收费怎么办？

有可能收费。

Unifi 官方目前明确把某些 underground + surface cabling 列为 Non-Standard Installation，并列出 RM212 Cabling Charge。

(Source: Unifi — Home Broadband Installation Journey)

Unifi — Installation Guide (unifi.com.my)

Maxis 也说明某些 Non-Standard Installation 会产生额外费用。

(Source: Maxis — Fibre Installation FAQs)

Maxis — Installation FAQ (maxis.com.my)

所以消费者在接受 Alternative Route 前，最好要求 ISP 确认：

  1. Installation Method；
  2. Cable Length；
  3. Underground / Surface Work；
  4. 是否需要新 Pole；
  5. Additional Charges；
  6. 谁负责相关工程。

先确认费用，再让他们施工。

应该保存什么证据？

如果你认为 Fibre 路线有问题，不要只靠电话投诉。

保存：

Pole 照片

拍下 Pole 和周围房屋。

DP 照片

如果 DP 在安全、允许拍摄的位置。

Cable Route 照片

清楚显示 Installer 打算怎么拉线。

Roof / Tree 照片

如果它们是争议的重点，就拍下来。

Property Boundary

让 ISP 看得出 Cable 为什么需要经过邻居范围。

所有沟通记录

包括：

  1. WhatsApp；
  2. SMS；
  3. Email；
  4. Installation Ticket；
  5. Order Number；
  6. Installer 的回复；
  7. Customer Service 的回复；
  8. Quotation；
  9. 照片。

这些资料以后投诉时非常有用。

ISP 不解决，可以投诉 MCMC 吗？

可以。

不过建议先给 ISP 一个合理的机会处理。

如果一直没有解决，可以通过 MCMC/CFM 的消费者投诉机制进行升级。

CFM 的投诉渠道涵盖包括 Service Delivery 和 Terms & Conditions Disputes 在内的通讯服务问题。

(Source: CFM — Complaint Channels)

CFM — Complaint Channels (cfm.my)

消费者可以通过 MCMC Consumer Redress Portal 提交投诉，也可以联系：

MCMC Consumer Care Centre：1800-188-030

(Source: CFM — New Complaint)

CFM — New Complaint / MCMC Consumer Redress Portal (cfm.my)

投诉时不要只写：

“ISP 不给我装 Fibre。”

应该把完整过程写出来。

例如：

“I applied for Fibre installation. The installer proposed an aerial cable route crossing a neighbouring private property. The neighbouring owner does not agree to the proposed route. I requested an alternative pole, DP or technical route assessment, but the issue remains unresolved.”

然后附上：

照片 + Ticket Number + WhatsApp + Email + ISP 回复。

这样投诉会清楚很多。

MCMC 会不会直接叫 ISP 搬 Pole？

不要这样预期。

投诉机制可以让消费者的服务问题进入正式处理流程，但并不代表 MCMC 会自动要求 ISP 在你指定的位置安装新 Pole。

实际解决方案仍然取决于：

  1. Network Infrastructure；
  2. DP 位置；
  3. Technical Feasibility；
  4. Installation Standard；
  5. Property Access；
  6. Construction Work；
  7. 相关审批。

CFM 的职责包括通过消费者投诉机制协助处理通讯服务相关投诉，并根据适用的消费者规范进行调解和解决。

(Source: CFM — About Us)

CFM — About Us (cfm.my)

所以投诉的目标应该是：

要求 ISP 对你的情况给出正式、合理的技术处理方案。

而不是直接要求监管机构帮你重新设计 Fibre network。

这些事情不要自己做

不要剪 Fibre Cable

即使你认为 Cable 经过你的范围，也不要自己剪。

直接向 ISP 投诉。

不要自己搬 Pole

Pole 属于 network infrastructure，不是屋主可以自行移动的东西。

不要砍邻居的树

即使树挡住 Fibre route，也不能因此自行处理邻居的财产。

不要先让他们安装，之后才投诉

如果你已经知道 Cable Route 有争议，最好在施工前解决。

不要只和 Installer 争论

涉及邻居、Pole、DP 或 Alternative Route 时，要求 ISP 的 technical/network team 介入。

最简单的处理流程

如果你的 Fibre installation 因邻居物业而出现问题，可以按照这个顺序：

1. 拍下 Proposed Route

Pole、DP、Roof、Tree、Property Boundary 全部记录。

2. 要求 Installer 记录问题

确保 Installation Ticket 有记录。

3. 联系 ISP

说明 proposed route 涉及邻居私人范围。

4. 要求 Technical Route Assessment

明确询问其他 Pole、DP 或 Fibre Route。

5. 询问 Alternative Installation

例如 Surface 或 Underground Cabling。

6. 询问费用

特别是 Non-Standard Installation。

7. 保存所有记录

WhatsApp、Email、Ticket、照片、Quotation 都保留。

8. ISP 仍然无法解决，再升级 MCMC/CFM

提交完整的时间线和证据。

可以直接发给 ISP 的投诉模板

如果你正在申请 Unifi、Maxis 或其他 Fibre，可以直接发送：

“The proposed Fibre installation route crosses a neighbouring private property / roof / tree, and the property owner does not agree to the proposed route. Please arrange a technical route assessment and advise whether an alternative pole, Distribution Point (DP), aerial route or other Fibre route is available. If an alternative installation is considered non-standard, please provide the installation method and applicable charges before proceeding.”

重点不是叫客服“换 Cable”。

而是要求：

Technical Route Assessment。

NetBijak's Take

Fibre 安装遇到邻居问题，首先应该把它当成一个 network route + installation issue，而不是邻居之间的私人战争。

目前没有足够依据告诉消费者：

“MCMC 规定 Fibre Cable 绝对不能跨邻居屋顶。”

这种说法太绝对。

更实际的处理方式是：

拍照记录 → 要求 ISP 重新检查路线 → 询问其他 Pole / DP → 要求 Alternative Route → 确认是否属于 Non-Standard Installation → 确认费用 → 无法解决再向 MCMC/CFM 投诉。

如果 proposed route 涉及邻居屋顶、树木或私人范围，不要自己砍树、搬 Pole 或剪 Fibre Cable。

消费者最有力的说法不是：

“MCMC 说你不能这样拉。”

而是：

“The proposed route crosses a neighbouring private property. Please conduct a technical route assessment and confirm whether an alternative pole, DP or Fibre route is available.”

这句话把问题交回 ISP 的 network team，让他们回答一个真正需要回答的问题：

有没有其他技术上可行的路线？

🎯为我找配套 →

title: Fibre Installation Crossing Neighbour Properties: How to Resolve Disputes
content:
If your Fibre installer wants to run a cable across your neighbour’s roof, tree or private property, do not simply accept the route or turn it into a dispute with your neighbour. Ask the ISP to document the proposed route, check whether an alternative pole or Fibre route is available, and clarify whether the proposed work is considered standard or non-standard installation.

The important point is that there is no simple MCMC consumer rule stating that every Fibre cable crossing a neighbouring property is automatically prohibited. In practice, the problem can involve the ISP’s network design, existing poles and Fibre Distribution Points (DPs), installation standards, access to property and whether another route is technically feasible.

Why Can a Fibre Installation Cross a Neighbour’s Property?

For landed homes, the Fibre connection normally has to travel from an existing network point to the customer’s house. Depending on the neighbourhood layout, the nearest pole or Fibre Distribution Point may not be directly in front of your property.

This can create situations where an installer proposes an aerial route that passes:

  1. over a neighbour’s roof;
  2. alongside or through a tree;
  3. above part of a neighbouring property;
  4. across a property boundary; or
  5. through an area where future maintenance may require access.

The existence of an existing pole does not automatically mean the proposed route is the only possible route.

That is why the first step should be to ask the ISP to assess the route, rather than arguing with the installer at your doorstep.

Does MCMC Prohibit Fibre Cables From Crossing a Neighbour’s Property?

This is where consumers should be careful.

We could not find an MCMC consumer rule that simply states:

“Fibre cables cannot cross a neighbour’s property.”

So NetBijak would not recommend telling homeowners that MCMC automatically prohibits every such installation.

Instead, the relevant consumer protection mechanism is the telecommunications complaint process.

The Communications and Multimedia Consumer Forum of Malaysia (CFM), which operates within the Malaysian communications and multimedia regulatory framework, accepts complaints involving issues such as Service Delivery, Terms & Conditions Disputes, Unfair Practice and Misrepresentation of Service. CFM — Complaint Channels

This means a disputed Fibre installation should first be treated as an ISP installation and service-delivery issue.

If the proposed route creates a genuine property-access problem, the practical question is:

Has the ISP properly assessed whether another technically feasible Fibre route is available?

What If the Fibre Cable Has to Cross Your Neighbour’s Roof?

This is one of the more sensitive situations for terrace-house owners.

Before installation proceeds, ask exactly what the installer intends to do.

Check:

  1. Where does the Fibre cable start?
  2. Which pole or DP is being used?
  3. Where will the cable enter your house?
  4. Will the cable pass over the neighbour’s roof?
  5. Will it be attached to the neighbour’s house?
  6. Will future repairs require access to the neighbour’s property?
  7. Is another pole or DP available?
  8. Has an alternative route been assessed?

Take photographs of the proposed route, including the pole, surrounding houses, roof, tree and property boundary.

Then contact the ISP and request a technical route assessment.

A useful request is:

“The proposed Fibre route crosses a neighbouring private property. Please arrange a technical route assessment and advise whether an alternative pole, Distribution Point (DP) or Fibre route is available.”

This is much stronger than simply telling customer service:

“I don't want the cable there.”

What If a Tree Is Blocking the Fibre Route?

A tree can create a bigger problem than a roof because the obstruction can change over time.

Branches can grow into the cable path, while strong winds, falling branches and tree maintenance can damage aerial Fibre.

If the proposed route passes through or depends on a neighbour’s tree, ask the ISP to confirm:

  1. whether the Fibre cable will contact the tree;
  2. whether sufficient clearance is available;
  3. whether the route can be changed;
  4. who is responsible if vegetation later damages the cable; and
  5. whether another pole or DP can be used.

Do not cut or remove your neighbour’s tree yourself simply to make the Fibre installation possible.

If vegetation needs to be removed or modified on another person’s property, clarify the responsibility and approval with the relevant property owner and ISP before work begins.

Can You Ask the ISP to Change the Pole Route?

Yes, you can request an alternative route assessment.

However, asking for a different route does not mean the ISP must automatically install a new pole wherever the customer wants.

The network team has to determine whether an alternative route is technically feasible.

Possible options may include:

  1. another existing pole;
  2. another Fibre Distribution Point;
  3. a different aerial route;
  4. surface cabling;
  5. underground cabling; or
  6. another technically feasible connection point.

The exact options depend on the infrastructure already available in the area.

What Does Unifi Consider Standard Installation?

Unifi’s current installation guide provides a useful example of how the distinction works.

It lists:

Direct cabling from pole directly to the Entry Wall

→ Standard Installation

→ Provided by TM

It also lists:

Pole to Entry Wall via underground and surface cabling

→ Non-Standard Installation

→ Customer bears the cost

→ Current stated cabling charge: RM212.

Unifi — Home Broadband Installation Journey

This matters because an alternative route may be technically possible but may not fall within the ISP’s standard installation scope.

Therefore, if an installer says:

“We can do it another way, but there is an additional charge,”

ask the ISP to explain why the alternative is classified as non-standard and what work the charge covers.

What About Maxis Fibre?

Maxis also distinguishes between standard and non-standard Fibre installation.

Its current installation FAQ states that standard installation covers the first 100 metres from the nearest Fibre Distribution Panel to the modem, using standard specifications such as cabling over the wall with clips.

Maxis states that additional charges may apply when the required cable length exceeds 100 metres, while non-standard installation methods such as over-ceiling cabling, underground ducts and concealed wiring are customer-borne costs.

Maxis — Fibre Installation FAQs

This gives consumers another important lesson:

An alternative installation method does not necessarily mean a free installation.

Always ask for the installation method and additional cost before approving the work.

What If the Neighbour Refuses?

If the neighbour clearly objects to the proposed Fibre route, do not force the installation.

Tell the ISP:

“The neighbouring property owner does not agree to the proposed Fibre route. Please assess whether an alternative pole, DP or Fibre route is available.”

Ask the ISP to record this in the installation ticket.

This is important because it turns the problem into a documented installation-route issue rather than a personal dispute between two homeowners.

If the ISP later says there is no alternative route, ask for an explanation:

  1. Why is the proposed route necessary?
  2. Was another pole checked?
  3. Was another DP checked?
  4. Was another aerial route assessed?
  5. Is underground or surface cabling possible?
  6. Would an alternative route involve additional charges?

Can You Ask for a New Fibre Pole?

You can request it, but you should frame the request as a technical assessment, not an unconditional demand.

Instead of saying:

“Move the pole.”

Use:

“The current pole position requires the proposed Fibre cable to cross a neighbouring private property. Please assess whether another pole, DP or network route can be used, and advise whether pole relocation is technically feasible.”

This gives the ISP’s network team several possible solutions to consider.

A new pole may involve network planning, infrastructure work and any applicable approvals, so it should not be presented to consumers as something an ISP is automatically required to provide.

What If the Installer Says “This Is the Only Route”?

Do not assume that the installer’s statement is necessarily the final network decision.

An installer may be working with the existing network infrastructure and the installation instructions available for that appointment.

If the proposed route creates a property or access dispute, ask the ISP to escalate the case to its technical or network team.

Use specific wording:

“Please escalate this installation for a technical route assessment. The proposed cable route crosses a neighbouring private property, and the property owner does not agree to the proposed route. Please confirm whether another pole, DP or Fibre route has been assessed.”

The objective is to move the discussion from:

Installer says no → Customer says no

to:

ISP technical team assesses the available network routes.

Will an Alternative Fibre Route Cost Extra?

It may.

Do not assume that every alternative route is included in standard installation.

For Unifi, the current installation guide explicitly classifies underground and surface cabling from the pole to the entry wall as non-standard and states a RM212 cabling charge.

Unifi Installation Guide — Standard vs Non-Standard Installation

For Maxis, non-standard methods such as underground ducts, concealed wiring and over-ceiling cabling can also incur additional costs.

Maxis Fibre Installation FAQ

Before approving an alternative route, ask the ISP for:

  1. installation method;
  2. estimated cable length;
  3. whether underground work is required;
  4. whether surface cabling is required;
  5. whether a new pole or other infrastructure is required;
  6. additional installation charges; and
  7. who is responsible for the work.

Get the cost confirmed before installation starts.

What Evidence Should You Keep?

If you think the proposed Fibre route is problematic, document it before the installer leaves.

Keep:

1. Photos of the pole

Show the pole and surrounding houses.

2. Photos of the Fibre DP

If the DP is visible and can be photographed safely.

3. Photos of the proposed cable route

Show where the installer intends to run the cable.

4. Photos of the roof or tree

Only where they are relevant to the proposed route.

5. Property boundary

Show why the proposed route crosses or depends on another property.

6. Installation records

Keep:

  1. installation appointment details;
  2. order number;
  3. service ticket number;
  4. WhatsApp messages;
  5. SMS;
  6. emails;
  7. installer comments;
  8. quotations; and
  9. photographs.

This documentation becomes particularly important if the ISP does not resolve the issue and you need to escalate the complaint.

When Should You Complain to MCMC/CFM?

The normal approach is to raise the issue with the ISP first.

If the issue remains unresolved, you can escalate through the MCMC/CFM consumer complaint mechanism.

CFM's complaint channels specifically include Service Delivery and Terms & Conditions Disputes, among other telecommunications-related complaint categories.

CFM — Complaint Channels

CFM's current complaint page states that consumers can submit complaints through the MCMC Consumer Redress Portal at aduan.mcmc.gov.my, by email, or through the MCMC Consumer Care Centre at 1800-188-030. The complaint service is provided free of charge.

CFM — New Complaint / MCMC Consumer Redress Portal

When escalating, do not simply write:

“ISP refuses to install Fibre.”

Give the complete history.

For example:

“I applied for Fibre installation on [date]. The installer proposed an aerial cable route crossing a neighbouring private property. The property owner does not agree to the proposed route. I requested an alternative pole, DP or technical route assessment, but the issue remains unresolved.”

Attach your photographs and previous communications.

That gives the complaint a clear service-delivery history.

What Can MCMC/CFM Actually Do?

Consumers should also have realistic expectations.

Submitting a complaint does not automatically mean MCMC will order an ISP to install a new pole at a location chosen by the customer.

The actual technical solution can depend on:

  1. existing network infrastructure;
  2. Fibre DP locations;
  3. technical feasibility;
  4. installation standards;
  5. property access;
  6. construction requirements; and
  7. any relevant approvals.

CFM states that its complaint-handling role includes providing channels for complaints covered by the General Consumer Code of Practice and handling complaints through mediation or resolution.

CFM — About Us / Complaint Handling

So the purpose of escalation is to obtain a proper response and resolution through the consumer redress process — not to assume that the regulator will automatically redesign the ISP's network.

What You Should NOT Do

Don't cut the Fibre cable

Even if you believe the cable is improperly routed, do not cut or interfere with telecommunications infrastructure.

Raise the issue with the ISP instead.

Don't move the pole

A telecommunications pole is network infrastructure. Request relocation or an alternative route through the ISP.

Don't cut your neighbour's tree

A Fibre installation dispute does not give you permission to modify another person's property.

Don't allow the installation first and complain later

If the route is clearly disputed, raise the issue before the cable is installed.

Don't rely only on the installer

If the problem involves another property, a pole or a possible alternative route, ask for the ISP's technical/network team to assess it.

The Practical Process: What to Do Step by Step

If your Fibre installation is blocked by a neighbour's property, follow this sequence.

Step 1 — Photograph the proposed route

Record the pole, DP, roof, tree and property boundary.

Step 2 — Ask the installer to document the issue

Make sure the installation ticket records why the installation cannot proceed.

Step 3 — Contact the ISP

Explain that the proposed route crosses or depends on a neighbouring private property.

Step 4 — Request a technical route assessment

Ask specifically about another pole, DP or Fibre route.

Step 5 — Ask about alternative installation methods

Find out whether surface or underground cabling is technically possible.

Step 6 — Ask about additional charges

Get any non-standard installation cost in writing before approving the work.

Step 7 — Keep the complete paper trail

Save ticket numbers, WhatsApp messages, emails, quotations and photographs.

Step 8 — Escalate if the issue remains unresolved

Use the MCMC/CFM consumer redress process and include the complete installation history.

Message Template to Send Your ISP

If you are dealing with Unifi, Maxis or another Fibre provider, you can use this wording:

“The proposed Fibre installation route crosses a neighbouring private property / roof / tree, and the property owner does not agree to the proposed route. Please arrange a technical route assessment and advise whether an alternative pole, Distribution Point (DP), aerial route or other Fibre route is available. If an alternative installation is considered non-standard, please provide the installation method and applicable charges before proceeding.”

This is much more effective than simply asking customer service to “change the cable”.

NetBijak's Take

A Fibre installation dispute involving a neighbour should be treated as a network-route and service-delivery issue first, not a personal argument between homeowners.

There is no basis for telling Malaysian consumers that MCMC has a blanket rule banning every Fibre cable from passing over a neighbouring property. The safer and more accurate approach is to examine the actual proposed route, the ISP's installation requirements and whether a technically feasible alternative exists.

For a landed property, the practical sequence is:

Document the route → ask the ISP to assess it → request an alternative pole/DP/route → clarify non-standard charges → escalate through MCMC/CFM if unresolved.

If the proposed route crosses a neighbour's roof or depends on a neighbour's tree, do not modify the neighbour's property and do not cut the Fibre cable yourself.

The strongest request is not:

“MCMC says this cable cannot cross my neighbour's house.”

It is:

“The proposed route crosses a neighbouring private property. Please conduct a technical route assessment and confirm whether an alternative pole, DP or Fibre route is available.”

That puts the issue back where it belongs: with the ISP's technical team to determine what network route is actually feasible.

title: WiFi 6 vs WiFi 7: Perlukah Anda Upgrade Router Broadband pada 2026?
content:
Jika anda sudah menggunakan Fibre 1Gbps atau 2Gbps, WiFi 7 memang boleh membantu mengurangkan Wireless Bottleneck — tetapi itu tidak bermaksud semua pengguna WiFi 6 perlu terus menukar Router.

Kelebihan utama WiFi 7 bukan sekadar nombor “maximum speed” yang lebih tinggi. Teknologi yang lebih penting ialah 320MHz Channel Width, 4096-QAM dan MLO (Multi-Link Operation).

Bagi pengguna Malaysia, soalan yang lebih penting ialah:

Adakah WiFi 7 benar-benar membantu anda menggunakan sepenuhnya sambungan Fibre 1Gbps atau 2Gbps di rumah?

WiFi 6 vs WiFi 7: Perbandingan Spesifikasi Utama

SpesifikasiWiFi 6 (802.11ax)WiFi 7 (802.11be)Kesan Kepada Penggunaan Sebenar
Maximum Channel WidthUp to 160MHzUp to 320MHzChannel yang lebih lebar boleh meningkatkan Wireless Throughput, terutama untuk Fibre berkelajuan tinggi dan NAS / Local Network
Modulation (QAM)1024-QAM4096-QAM (4K-QAM)Symbol Rate secara teori meningkat sekitar 20%, tetapi kelajuan sebenar bergantung pada Signal Quality dan sokongan peranti
Multi-Link Operation (MLO)Tidak menyokong MLO sebagai ciri WiFi 7Multi-Link OperationPeranti yang serasi boleh menggunakan beberapa Wireless Link untuk meningkatkan Throughput, mengurangkan Latency dan mengekalkan kestabilan
Typical Fibre Use Case100Mbps–1Gbps1Gbps–2Gbps+WiFi 7 lebih sesuai untuk Fibre berkelajuan tinggi, tetapi 2Gbps tetap memerlukan Multi-Gigabit Ethernet pada rangkaian yang berkaitan

Jangan anggap WiFi 7 bermaksud “dua kali lebih laju daripada WiFi 6” dalam semua keadaan.

WiFi 7 menggabungkan beberapa peningkatan teknologi untuk menyediakan lebih banyak Wireless Capacity dan kecekapan. Intel menyenaraikan 320MHz, 4096-QAM dan MLO sebagai antara teknologi utama WiFi 7. (Source: Intel — Wi-Fi 7 Series)

Apa Yang Sebenarnya Berubah Daripada WiFi 6 ke WiFi 7?

WiFi 7 ialah peningkatan kepada WiFi 6 dengan beberapa teknologi baharu yang direka untuk meningkatkan Throughput, Latency dan penggunaan Spectrum.

Antara ciri utama ialah:

  1. 320MHz Channel Width
  2. 4096-QAM
  3. Multi-Link Operation (MLO)
  4. Multi-RU Puncturing
  5. Kecekapan Wireless yang lebih tinggi

Untuk pengguna rumah, dua perkara paling penting ialah:

320MHz = Wireless Channel yang lebih lebar.

MLO = Peranti serasi boleh menggunakan beberapa Wireless Link dengan lebih fleksibel.

1. 320MHz: Peningkatan Terbesar Untuk Throughput

WiFi 6 menyokong Channel Width sehingga 160MHz.

WiFi 7 meningkatkannya sehingga 320MHz.

Cara paling mudah untuk faham ialah dengan membayangkan sebuah lebuh raya.

160MHz ibarat lebuh raya dengan jumlah lorong tertentu.

320MHz pula memberikan ruang yang lebih luas untuk data bergerak pada masa yang sama.

Ini amat berguna untuk:

  1. Pemindahan fail besar
  2. NAS
  3. PC-to-PC file transfer
  4. Video bitrate tinggi
  5. Local Media Server
  6. Fibre berkelajuan tinggi
  7. Banyak peranti berprestasi tinggi

Tetapi 320MHz tidak bermaksud telefon anda secara automatik akan mendapat kelajuan dua kali ganda.

Router dan Client Device perlu menyokong teknologi yang diperlukan.

Selain itu, prestasi sebenar dipengaruhi oleh:

  1. Jarak dari Router
  2. Dinding
  3. Interference
  4. Channel availability
  5. Signal Quality

Channel yang lebih lebar juga tidak semestinya lebih baik dalam semua rumah.

Jika kawasan anda mempunyai banyak WiFi berdekatan, penggunaan Channel yang sangat lebar boleh menghadapi lebih banyak gangguan.

Jadi, 320MHz paling berguna apabila:

Router dan Client menyokong WiFi 7, dan keadaan Wireless di lokasi penggunaan cukup baik.

2. 4096-QAM: Lebih Banyak Data Dalam Setiap Transmission

WiFi 6 menggunakan 1024-QAM.

WiFi 7 pula menggunakan 4096-QAM atau 4K-QAM.

QAM yang lebih tinggi membolehkan lebih banyak data dikodkan dalam setiap Symbol.

Dalam keadaan ideal, 4096-QAM boleh memberikan peningkatan sekitar 20% pada Symbol Rate berbanding 1024-QAM.

Tetapi jangan terjemahkan angka itu kepada:

“WiFi 7 mesti 20% lebih laju.”

Throughput sebenar masih bergantung kepada Signal Quality, Channel Width, Spatial Streams, Interference serta kemampuan Router dan Client.

4096-QAM paling berguna apabila:

Signal kuat, jarak dekat dengan Router dan persekitaran Wireless tidak terlalu sesak.

Sebab itu peningkatan mungkin lebih ketara di ruang tamu atau bilik yang dekat dengan Router berbanding bilik yang dipisahkan oleh beberapa dinding.

3. MLO: Ciri WiFi 7 Yang Paling Menarik Untuk Penggunaan Sebenar

Jika 320MHz menjadikan Wireless Channel lebih lebar, MLO (Multi-Link Operation) pula mengubah cara peranti menggunakan Wireless Link.

Dengan MLO, peranti WiFi 7 yang serasi boleh menggunakan beberapa Wireless Link bergantung kepada Router, Client dan konfigurasi.

Ini boleh membantu meningkatkan:

  1. Throughput
  2. Latency
  3. Connection Stability
  4. Ketahanan apabila salah satu Link mengalami Interference
  5. Prestasi dalam rangkaian yang sibuk

Intel menerangkan MLO sebagai ciri WiFi 7 yang membolehkan peranti serasi menggunakan beberapa Link untuk meningkatkan Throughput, Latency dan Reliability. (Source: Intel — Wi-Fi 7 Series)

Kenapa MLO berguna untuk rumah Malaysia?

Bayangkan satu rumah mempunyai:

  1. Seseorang sedang bermain Online Game
  2. TV sedang menonton Netflix 4K
  3. Laptop sedang melakukan Cloud Backup
  4. NAS sedang memindahkan fail
  5. Beberapa Smartphone sedang digunakan
  6. Smart Home Devices sentiasa connected

Dalam keadaan seperti ini, masalah mungkin bukan Fibre.

Masalahnya ialah Wireless Network sedang sibuk.

MLO memberi peranti yang serasi lebih banyak fleksibiliti untuk menggunakan Wireless Link yang tersedia.

Tetapi ada satu perkara penting:

Router dan Client perlu menyokong MLO.

Dan MLO bukan bermaksud 2.4GHz + 5GHz + 6GHz akan sentiasa dicampurkan dan memberikan jumlah maximum speed ketiga-tiganya.

Adakah WiFi 7 Berbaloi Untuk Fibre 1Gbps?

Ini bahagian paling penting untuk pengguna Malaysia.

Katakan anda melanggan Fibre 1Gbps.

Sambungan Fibre anda boleh memberikan sehingga sekitar 1Gbps, tetapi itu tidak bermaksud setiap Smartphone atau Laptop akan mendapat 1Gbps melalui WiFi.

Rantaian rangkaian anda sebenarnya kelihatan seperti ini:

Fibre → ONT / Gateway → Router → WiFi → Client Device

Jika salah satu bahagian menjadi Bottleneck, prestasi akhir akan terjejas.

Router WiFi 6 yang baik masih mampu memberikan Wireless Throughput yang tinggi dalam keadaan yang sesuai.

Jadi:

WiFi 6 → WiFi 7 ialah Wireless Performance Upgrade, bukan Fibre Speed Upgrade.

Anda mungkin mendapat Speed Test yang lebih tinggi, tetapi peningkatannya bergantung kepada peranti dan keadaan Wireless di rumah.

Pengguna 1Gbps Mana Yang Patut Pertimbangkan WiFi 7?

1. Anda Sudah Mempunyai Beberapa WiFi 7 Devices

Contohnya:

  1. WiFi 7 Laptop
  2. WiFi 7 Smartphone
  3. WiFi 7 Desktop Adapter

Jika Client anda sudah menyokong WiFi 7, barulah Router WiFi 7 boleh digunakan sepenuhnya.

Jika semua peranti anda masih WiFi 5 atau WiFi 6, menukar Router sahaja tidak akan menjadikan peranti tersebut WiFi 7.

2. Ramai Pengguna Menggunakan Internet Pada Masa Yang Sama

Contohnya:

  1. Beberapa 4K Streaming
  2. Gaming
  3. Video Call
  4. Cloud Backup
  5. NAS
  6. Download fail besar

Dalam keadaan seperti ini, tambahan Wireless Capacity WiFi 7 boleh membantu.

3. Anda Banyak Menggunakan NAS atau Local Network

Ini sering terlepas daripada perhatian pengguna Broadband.

Jika anda kerap memindahkan Video, gambar atau Backup berkapasiti besar antara PC dan NAS, masalah mungkin bukan kelajuan Internet.

Local WiFi Network mungkin menjadi Bottleneck.

Dalam keadaan ini, 320MHz dan WiFi 7 Client boleh memberikan manfaat yang lebih ketara berbanding penggunaan biasa seperti Browsing atau Streaming.

Bagaimana Dengan Fibre 2Gbps?

Untuk 2Gbps, kes WiFi 7 menjadi lebih kuat.

Sebabnya mudah.

Jika mana-mana Network Component hanya menyokong 1Gbps, komponen tersebut boleh menjadi Bottleneck.

Contohnya:

2Gbps Fibre → 1GbE Router Port → Maximum sekitar 1Gbps

Jadi Router WiFi 7 yang mahal tidak akan menyelesaikan masalah jika Wired Link anda sendiri hanya 1GbE.

Untuk Fibre 2Gbps, periksa keseluruhan rangkaian:

Fibre → ONT / Gateway → Router → Ethernet → WiFi → Client

Perkara yang perlu diperiksa termasuk:

  1. WAN Port
  2. LAN Port
  3. Ethernet Cable
  4. Router Performance
  5. WiFi Standard
  6. Client Adapter
  7. Mesh Backhaul

Jika komputer anda hanya mempunyai 1GbE LAN Port, komputer tersebut tidak akan menggunakan lebih daripada 1Gbps melalui sambungan Wired tersebut walaupun Router anda menyokong 2.5GbE atau lebih tinggi.

Sebab itu:

2Gbps Fibre + WiFi 7 tidak bermaksud setiap peranti akan mendapat 2Gbps.

ISP Malaysia Sudah Mula Menawarkan WiFi 7

WiFi 7 bukan lagi sekadar teknologi untuk Router Retail kelas tinggi.

Pada 2026, beberapa ISP Malaysia sudah menawarkan WiFi 7 bersama pakej Fibre berkelajuan tinggi.

CelcomDigi kini menawarkan WiFi 7 Router dalam beberapa pelan Fibre dan menyediakan Premium WiFi 7 Router serta Mesh Node pada pelan berkelajuan lebih tinggi. (Source: CelcomDigi — Fibre Home Broadband)

TIME pula menawarkan WiFi 7 dalam beberapa pelan Fibre berkelajuan tinggi, manakala pelan yang lebih rendah masih menggunakan WiFi 6. (Source: TIME — Fibre Broadband)

Unifi juga menawarkan peralatan WiFi 7 dan pilihan Mesh untuk pengguna Fibre berkelajuan tinggi. (Source: Unifi — Home Fibre)

Jadi pada 2026, persoalannya bukan lagi:

“Adakah Malaysia sudah ada WiFi 7?”

Persoalan sebenar ialah:

“Adakah rumah saya akan mendapat manfaat daripada WiFi 7?”

Siapa Yang Patut Upgrade Ke WiFi 7?

Upgrade jika:

Anda sedang beralih kepada Fibre 2Gbps

Ini ialah sebab paling jelas.

2Gbps memerlukan lebih daripada sekadar Fibre yang laju. Home Network anda juga perlu menyokong Multi-Gigabit.

Anda sudah mempunyai WiFi 7 Devices

Jika Laptop, Smartphone dan Desktop Adapter utama anda menyokong WiFi 7, upgrade Router lebih masuk akal.

WiFi menjadi Bottleneck

Jika:

Wired Speed Test ≈ Fibre Plan Speed

tetapi:

WiFi Speed Test jauh lebih rendah

anda patut menyiasat Wireless Network.

WiFi 7 mungkin membantu, tetapi jangan terus membeli Router baharu sebelum memeriksa Router Placement, Channel, Interference dan Client Device.

Anda pengguna NAS / Power User

WiFi 7 lebih menarik jika anda:

  1. Memindahkan fail besar
  2. Membuat Backup melalui rangkaian
  3. Menggunakan NAS
  4. Mengedit Video
  5. Memindahkan data antara beberapa PC

Siapa Yang Tidak Perlu Upgrade Lagi?

Jika anda menggunakan:

  1. Fibre 100Mbps–300Mbps
  2. Kebanyakan peranti masih WiFi 5 / WiFi 6
  3. Apartment kecil
  4. Netflix / YouTube / Browsing biasa
  5. Tiada NAS
  6. Tiada Local File Transfer yang besar
  7. Tiada masalah WiFi Congestion

tidak ada sebab yang kuat untuk menggantikan Router WiFi 6 yang masih berfungsi dengan baik.

Malah untuk pengguna biasa:

Selesaikan masalah rangkaian sebenar dahulu sebelum mengejar standard WiFi terbaru.

Sebelum Upgrade WiFi 7, Periksa 5 Perkara Ini

1. Router Placement

Router WiFi 7 yang diletakkan di dalam kabinet atau di sudut rumah masih boleh menghasilkan Coverage yang lemah.

Letakkan Router di lokasi yang lebih central, tinggi dan kurang terhalang jika boleh.

2. Client Device

Router WiFi 7 tidak akan menjadikan Smartphone WiFi 6 sebagai Smartphone WiFi 7.

Client Device perlu menyokong WiFi 7 untuk menggunakan ciri baharu tersebut.

3. Ethernet Port

Ini sangat penting untuk pengguna 2Gbps.

1GbE boleh menjadi Bottleneck kepada sambungan 2Gbps.

Jika anda mahu menggunakan kelajuan Multi-Gigabit, semak sama ada Router dan Client mempunyai 2.5GbE atau Ethernet yang lebih pantas.

4. Mesh Backhaul

WiFi 7 Mesh tidak bermaksud setiap bilik akan mendapat prestasi yang sama seperti Main Router.

Jika Mesh Node menggunakan Wireless Backhaul, Backhaul itu sendiri menggunakan Wireless Capacity.

Jika boleh menarik kabel:

Wired Ethernet Backhaul biasanya pilihan yang lebih konsisten.

5. Speed Test

Speed Test dipengaruhi oleh lebih daripada Fibre anda.

Antaranya:

  1. WiFi Signal
  2. Client Hardware
  3. Router
  4. Ethernet Port
  5. Test Server
  6. Internet Routing
  7. Background Traffic

Jangan terus menyalahkan WiFi 6 hanya kerana satu Speed Test menunjukkan kelajuan lebih rendah daripada pakej anda.

WiFi 6 vs WiFi 7: Berbaloi Upgrade Atau Tidak?

SituasiWiFi 6 → WiFi 7Pandangan NetBijak
Fibre 100–300MbpsManfaat rendahKekal dengan WiFi 6
Fibre 500MbpsBiasanya rendahUpgrade hanya jika ada masalah tertentu
1Gbps + WiFi 6 DevicesSederhanaWiFi 6 masih mencukupi
1Gbps + banyak WiFi 7 DevicesBerbaloi dipertimbangkanLebih banyak Wireless Headroom
2Gbps + 1GbE NetworkSelesaikan Ethernet Bottleneck dahuluJangan upgrade WiFi sahaja
2Gbps + Multi-Gigabit Network + WiFi 7 DevicesPotensi manfaat tinggiKes penggunaan terbaik untuk WiFi 7
NAS / Large Local File TransferPotensi tinggi320MHz lebih bermakna
Rumah besar + WiFi CongestionBergantung keadaanMLO + Mesh yang direka dengan betul boleh membantu

Perlukah Anda Tukar Router Pada 2026?

Bagi kebanyakan pengguna, tidak perlu tergesa-gesa.

Jika Router WiFi 6 anda masih memberikan:

  1. Coverage yang baik
  2. Kelajuan mencukupi
  3. Latency yang normal
  4. Connection yang stabil

tiada keperluan mendesak untuk menggantikannya hanya kerana WiFi 7 ialah standard baharu.

Tetapi jika anda:

  1. Upgrade kepada Fibre 1Gbps / 2Gbps
  2. Membeli Router baharu
  3. Mempunyai banyak WiFi 7 Devices
  4. Menggunakan NAS
  5. Mengalami WiFi Congestion
  6. Membina Mesh Network baharu

WiFi 7 lebih wajar dipertimbangkan.

Ada satu rule yang sangat mudah untuk pengguna Malaysia:

Jika ISP anda sudah memberikan WiFi 7 Router sebagai sebahagian daripada pakej tanpa kos perkakasan tambahan, gunakan sahaja.

Tidak banyak sebab untuk sengaja memilih hardware WiFi 6 yang lebih lama jika WiFi 7 sudah termasuk dalam pakej.

Tetapi jika anda perlu membayar ratusan ringgit untuk menggantikan Router WiFi 6 yang masih berfungsi dengan baik, pastikan upgrade tersebut menyelesaikan masalah sebenar.

NetBijak's Take

WiFi 7 bukan sebab untuk upgrade Fibre. Ia ialah teknologi yang membantu anda menggunakan sambungan Fibre berkelajuan tinggi dengan lebih baik melalui Wireless Network.

Untuk pengguna 300Mbps dan ke bawah, Router WiFi 6 yang baik biasanya sudah mencukupi.

Untuk 500Mbps, WiFi 6 masih pilihan yang munasabah kecuali anda menghadapi masalah Coverage, Congestion atau Local Network.

Untuk 1Gbps, WiFi 7 mula menjadi lebih menarik apabila anda mempunyai WiFi 7 Devices, ramai pengguna serentak atau penggunaan NAS / Local Network yang berat.

Untuk 2Gbps, alasan untuk menggunakan WiFi 7 menjadi lebih kuat.

Tetapi jangan lihat Router sahaja.

Keseluruhan rangkaian perlu mampu mengendalikan kelajuan tersebut:

Fibre → Multi-Gigabit Ethernet → WiFi 7 Router → WiFi 7 Client

Dan dua ciri WiFi 7 yang paling penting untuk diingati ialah:

320MHz = Wireless Capacity yang lebih besar.

MLO = penggunaan beberapa Wireless Link dengan lebih fleksibel.

Jadi soalan terbaik pada 2026 bukan:

“Adakah WiFi 7 lebih laju daripada WiFi 6?”

Tetapi:

“Adakah Fibre, peranti dan Home Network saya sudah sampai ke tahap WiFi 6 menjadi Bottleneck?”

Jika belum, kekalkan WiFi 6.

Jika anda sudah menggunakan 1Gbps / 2Gbps Fibre + WiFi 7 Devices + penggunaan rangkaian yang berat, barulah upgrade WiFi 7 benar-benar masuk akal.
